mn_keyhole_area.blurb: Keyhole Area is a small cluster of cliffs on the Minnesota bank of the St. Croix River at Taylors Falls, part of the traditional-only gorge climbing there. Most of the eleven lines are gear-protected leads, with a couple set up purely as top ropes. Grades start around 5.6 and stretch to 5.11, with the bulk of them in the middle of that range, so it suits a mixed party better than a pure beginner outing. Expect short, clean walls of dark volcanic rock, protection placed by hand, and a walk in along the river trail from the north-end lot. The tops are reached by a chimney system on the north side of the overlook.

mn_angle_rock.blurb: Angle Rock is a small point of rock poking into the St. Croix River at Taylors Falls. It has two distinct faces, one looking up toward the bridge and town and the other looking down across the water to Wisconsin. Walls are around 30 feet, so these are short outings, and a big boulder on top gives a convenient anchor for top ropes. Of the eleven lines, most are trad leads and a few are top-rope, with grades from about 5.6 up to 5.12 and a good number in the 5.10 range. The river keeps it cool and it is quieter than neighbouring sectors, though passing tour boats mean an audience.

mn_5_saturday_buttress.blurb: Saturday Buttress is one of the busier buttresses on the Prairie Walls, the quartzite cliff line in Blue Mounds State Park near Luverne in the far southwest corner of Minnesota. It sits between two neighbouring buttresses and holds eleven routes, mostly top-rope with a few trad leads. Grades are moderate: nearly everything falls between 5.5 and 5.9, with the largest group at 5.8, which makes it a friendly place for newer climbers and for sessions with a group. The wall faces east, giving morning sun and some evening shade. A chimney at the far left end is the usual scramble to reach the anchors.
mn_5_saturday_buttress.parking_note: Use the small lot off Rock County 8 (141st St.), reached by turning east from the highway and driving about a mile and a quarter; it is on the left.
mn_5_saturday_buttress.approach: From the lot, follow the paved bike and walking path about three quarters of a mile until the cliff comes into view, then take a short trail through the grass to the base.
